grammar.0.title: From 0 to 20
grammar.0.intro: Tap and listen. As in Bangla, 11–19 each have their own word.
grammar.0.note: 16 = sechzehn (sechs loses its s), 17 = siebzehn (sieben loses its en).
grammar.1.title: Tens, hundred, thousand
grammar.1.intro: Twenty, thirty… a hundred, a thousand.
grammar.2.title: 21 to 99: reversed order!
grammar.2.intro: German says the units first, then “und”, then the tens — 21 = “one and twenty”.
grammar.2.note: Above 100 it is normal: 125 = hundertfünfundzwanzig. Phone numbers are usually said in pairs.
grammar.3.title: Saying years
grammar.3.text: Years are said like this: 1995 = neunzehnhundertfünfundneunzig (19 hundred + 95); 2024 = zweitausendvierundzwanzig (two thousand + 24). For age: “Ich bin 22 Jahre alt.” or simply “Ich bin 22.”
quiz.3.prompt: How do you say 45 in German?
quiz.3.why: Units first (fünf), then und, then the tens (vierzig).
quiz.5.prompt: What does “Wie alt bist du?” ask?
quiz.6.prompt: Put the words in order: “I am 22 years old.”
quiz.7.why: Wie alt bist du? = How old are you?
dialog.0.de.1.n: alt = old; Wie alt = how old
dialog.1.de.2.n: zwei + und + zwanzig: units first, then tens
